summary: What every page of a swarm.press site is held to, rendered in a browser at a desktop's and a phone's width (ADR-0094). The same for every site. Deterministic rules block a release on any finding outside a listed content gap; judged rules block it below their threshold once the owner has calibrated them.

rules.summary: The page renders: it answers 200 and loads in the browser.

No empty picture frame: a picture box (an image block, a card's picture, a featured image, a tile) with no picture, no background and next to no text in it. An entry without a picture shows the text-only variant.
Every picture shown loads: no picture whose file is missing or is not a picture.
Every picture that is not marked decorative says what it shows (alt text).
A picture's alt text is not the page's title, its SEO title or the site's title: it describes the picture.
No link to `#`, to nothing or to script: every link and button goes somewhere.
Every link inside the site goes to a page the release has.
Every in-page link (`#section`) has its target on the page.
No request of the page fails (an answer of 400 or more, or no answer).
A release serves itself: no request goes to the production host it will replace (a preview that does depends on the old site).
The static export carries none of WordPress's runtime extras: no emoji script, emoji styles or emoji settings.
Nothing is wider than a phone's screen: no sideways scrolling at 390 px.
At 1280 px no block sits in under 75% of its page's container with nothing beside it (a half-empty row). A story's text keeps its reading measure and is exempt.
Exactly one h1 is shown.
The h1 is the page's own: the authored hero's title when the page has one, else the page's own title block, else a heading that names the page's title.
Headings go down one level at a time (no h2 then h4) outside the header, the footer and the menus.
A page's authored hero comes first in its content: no listing, filter bar or card grid before it.
No chip, badge, eyebrow, filter or tag shows a slug (`church`, `getting-here`): labels are words.
On a page in another language, none of the design's own words is left in English.
The page has a title of a sane length.
The page has a meta description of a sane length.
The page names itself as canonical, on the site's public origin.
On a site in several languages each page lists its language versions (hreflang), itself included; every version listed exists and lists it back.
The site has a sitemap and every indexable page is in it.
No two pages share a title.
A picture shows what its section is about (vision, a fixed rubric). Not judged before step 5 of ADR-0094; its threshold is frozen after the owner's spot check.
The page's copy holds the editorial bar (a fixed rubric). Not judged before step 5 of ADR-0094.
A page type looks like its design family: its Claude Design page, or the style guide for a type marked derived (vision, a fixed rubric). Not judged before step 5 of ADR-0094.

changes: empty-frame: a box needs both sides of min_side_px (48) to be a picture frame; a chip row left where a card has no picture (350 x 30) is not one
h1-own: the page's own title block (post-title, query-title) is the page's own h1 by construction; the fuzzy match against the document title applies to any other h1
